comment: Single source of the K4 durable store format and of the managed-state
service protocol. tools/gen_k4_format.py derives from this file the Rust
module the service encodes with, the Python module the gate decodes with,
and the byte fixtures both are checked against; tools/check_k4_format.py
regenerates and compares. Nothing in user/k4fmt/src/generated.rs or in
Generating both sides does not make them agree by argument: they share
offsets, so of course they agree about those. What the arrangement buys is
that neither the service nor the gate defines the format. The bytes on the
medium are the ones this file specifies; the digests are computed by a
hand-written SHA-256 inside the guest and by hashlib on the host, and the
golden vectors this file fixes are what both are held to.
Every structure is little-endian with explicit padding; a field that would
need implicit padding is a schema error rather than something the
A digest prefix is the listed ASCII bytes followed by one zero byte, so a
raw byte object and a tree can never occupy the same unlabelled space.

RecordKind.name: CHECKPOINT
RecordKind.doc: Opens an arena: published root, high-water marks, retained roots.

RecordKind.name: PREPARE
RecordKind.doc: A publication request that has been admitted and may not be forgotten.

RecordKind.name: COMMIT
RecordKind.doc: The transition that makes a new generation the published one.

RecordKind.name: ABORT
RecordKind.doc: A prepared request that will not commit.

RecordKind.name: OUTBOX
RecordKind.doc: What a broker reported about an intent committed with a publication.

ObjectType.name: POLICY
ObjectType.doc: Who may publish and what evidence a publication requires.

ObjectType.name: VALIDATION
ObjectType.doc: A limited claim about named inputs and a named version.

ObjectType.name: RECEIPT
ObjectType.doc: What a publication was: request, inputs, generation.

StoreOp.name: QUERY
StoreOp.doc: Published generation, root, durable extent and free capacity.

StoreOp.name: READ
StoreOp.doc: Bytes of one object of one version, with a bounded retention.

StoreOp.name: FORK
StoreOp.doc: A private workspace over a version.

StoreOp.name: WRITE
StoreOp.doc: Bind a name to an object inside a private workspace.

StoreOp.name: FREEZE
StoreOp.doc: Turn a workspace into an immutable candidate root.

StoreOp.name: PUBLISH
StoreOp.doc: Ask for a conditioned transition of the published root.

StoreOp.name: RESULT
StoreOp.doc: The durable answer for a request identity, or explicit uncertainty.

StoreOp.name: DISCARD
StoreOp.doc: Release a workspace once its readers and operations are done.

StoreOp.name: PUT_OBJECT
StoreOp.doc: Stage an immutable object; returns its content digest.

StoreOp.name: RETAIN
StoreOp.doc: Hold a version against reuse for a bounded time.

StoreOp.name: COMPACT
StoreOp.doc: Maintenance: copy the reachable set to the other arena.

StoreOp.name: HARNESS
StoreOp.doc: Report the fault directive this run was started with. Scaffolding.

StoreOp.name: STATS
StoreOp.doc: Counters the service recovered or accumulated.

StoreStatus.name: FORBIDDEN
StoreStatus.doc: The authenticated facet does not carry this authority.

StoreStatus.name: GENERATION_STALE
StoreStatus.doc: The expected generation is not the published one.

StoreStatus.name: VALIDATION_MISMATCH
StoreStatus.doc: The evidence does not name these inputs or this version.

StoreStatus.name: CONFLICT
StoreStatus.doc: That request identity was already used for different inputs.

StoreStatus.name: SEQUENCE_GAP
StoreStatus.doc: The previous request of this principal is unresolved.

StoreStatus.name: RESULT_EXPIRED
StoreStatus.doc: Resolved and evicted: neither commit nor abort is asserted.

StoreStatus.name: EXHAUSTED
StoreStatus.doc: Admitting would eat the reserve recovery and closure need.

StoreStatus.name: EFFECT_REFUSED
StoreStatus.doc: The kernel refused to admit the effect: a barrier won the race.

StoreStatus.name: INTEGRITY_FAILED
StoreStatus.doc: A prefix that was supposed to be durable did not verify.

StoreStatus.name: RETAINED
StoreStatus.doc: Readers or retentions still name it.

ResultOutcome.name: NEVER_SEEN
ResultOutcome.doc: No durable trace of that request identity.

ResultOutcome.name: UNKNOWN
ResultOutcome.doc: Durably prepared and not resolved: neither outcome may be asserted.

OutboxStatus.name: DELIVERED
OutboxStatus.doc: The broker acknowledged this idempotency key.

OutboxStatus.name: UNKNOWN
OutboxStatus.doc: The attempt neither succeeded nor is known to have failed.

OutboxStatus.name: REFUSED
OutboxStatus.doc: The broker answered that it will not accept it.

AbortReason.name: RECOVERED_UNRESOLVED
AbortReason.doc: Prepared, never committed, resolved by recovery.

AbortReason.name: DEPENDENCY_MISSING
AbortReason.doc: A commit existed but an object it names does not.

FaultMode.name: STOP
FaultMode.doc: Issue nothing further and end the machine at the named point.

FaultMode.name: DROP_WRITE
FaultMode.doc: Never issue the write at the named point; carry on as if it had been.

FaultMode.name: TEAR_WRITE
FaultMode.doc: Issue only the first sector of that record, then stop.

FaultMode.name: LOSE_RESPONSE
FaultMode.doc: Complete durably and end the machine before the caller is answered.

FaultMode.name: KILL_SERVICE
FaultMode.doc: Stop the service domain at the named point; the machine keeps running.

FaultMode.name: IO_ERROR
FaultMode.doc: The medium refuses the write at the named point. A service may not publish on a state it only assumes.

FaultMode.name: REORDER
FaultMode.doc: Hold the write at the named point and issue it after the next one, so an unflushed sequence is not the order the medium sees.

FaultPoint.name: BEFORE_OBJECT
FaultPoint.doc: At the object whose ordinal is the fault argument.

FaultPoint.name: AFTER_COMMIT
FaultPoint.doc: The commit is durable; nothing after it is.

FaultPoint.name: AFTER_CHECKPOINT
FaultPoint.doc: The new arena is written; the superblock has not switched.

FaultPoint.name: AFTER_SUPERBLOCK
FaultPoint.doc: The switch is durable; the old arena has not been reused.

structs.name: StoreSuperblock
structs.doc: One of two alternating superblocks. The valid one with the highest generation selects the arena.

fields.name: store_uuid
fields.doc: Identity of this store, so a restored copy is not mistaken for continuity.

fields.name: store_epoch
fields.doc: Format and administrative recovery epoch.

fields.name: superblock_generation
fields.doc: Strictly increasing; the newest complete one wins.

fields.name: checkpoint_sequence
fields.doc: Sequence of the checkpoint that opens the active arena.

fields.name: durable_through_sequence
fields.doc: Lower bound on what was durable when this was written. A shorter valid prefix is an integrity failure, not a torn tail.

fields.name: digest
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the preceding bytes of this superblock.

structs.name: RecordHeader
structs.doc: Header of every framed record. A record occupies whole blocks, so a torn write damages its own record and never one already durable.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: RecordKind.

fields.name: sequence
fields.doc: Increases by exactly one within an arena.

fields.name: prev_digest
fields.doc: Digest of the preceding record; zero for the first of an arena.

fields.name: digest
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the header up to this field, then of payload_len payload bytes.

structs.name: ObjectRecordHeader
structs.doc: Payload head of an OBJECT record; the canonical bytes follow it.

fields.name: content_digest
fields.doc: The canonical object digest, recomputed on recovery rather than believed.

structs.name: PrepareRecord
structs.doc: Payload of PREPARE: everything that decides what this publication means.

fields.name: request_digest
fields.doc: Digest of every input that affects the meaning of the request.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0: an outbox intent is committed with this publication.

fields.name: invocation_id
fields.doc: The invocation whose effect admission authorised beginning this.

structs.name: CommitRecord
structs.doc: Payload of COMMIT. Adopted only when its prepare and every object it depends on are in the same valid prefix.

fields.name: object_count
fields.doc: Objects written between the prepare and this commit.

structs.name: AbortRecord
structs.doc: Payload of ABORT: a prepared identity that will never commit.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: AbortReason.

structs.name: CheckpointRecord
structs.doc: Payload head of CHECKPOINT; principal, result and retained entries follow in that order.

fields.name: object_count
fields.doc: Objects copied into this arena after the checkpoint.

structs.name: PrincipalEntry
structs.doc: A principal's durable high-water mark and its at most one pending request.

fields.name: high_water
fields.doc: Highest resolved request sequence.

fields.name: pending_sequence
fields.doc: Prepared and unresolved, or zero.

structs.name: ResultEntry
structs.doc: A recent durable result. Evicting one turns a later query into RESULT_EXPIRED, which asserts neither commit nor abort.

structs.name: RetainedEntry
structs.doc: A root held against reuse until its expiry.

structs.name: OutboxRecord
structs.doc: Payload of OUTBOX: what a broker reported about an intent. UNKNOWN is a result, not a failure to record one.

fields.name: request_digest
fields.doc: The idempotency key the broker was given.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: OutboxStatus.

structs.name: HarnessDirective
structs.doc: Scaffolding. Written by the host into a block outside the store and read once at startup; recovery never consults it and no format rule depends on it.

fields.name: stop_at_next_flush
fields.doc: Scaffolding: 1 makes the service end the run where it would have flushed next, so a mode that only matters before a flush can be observed after one.

structs.name: TreeHeader
structs.doc: Canonical head of a TREE object; entries follow, ordered by name bytes.

structs.name: TreeEntry
structs.doc: One binding. Names are unique, non-empty, carry no NUL and no separator, and are never normalised.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0: executable. Part of the version, not metadata beside it.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Bytes past name_len must be zero.

structs.name: Manifest
structs.doc: Canonical bytes of a root: the content, the policy it was published under, and the evidence offered for it.

structs.name: Policy
structs.doc: Canonical bytes of a policy: who may publish, and what evidence a publication must carry.

fields.name: publish_principals
fields.doc: Bit per principal. Authority comes from the facet; this only narrows it further.

structs.name: Validation
structs.doc: Canonical bytes of a limited claim: this tool, this configuration, these inputs, that version.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: 1 pass, 2 fail.

fields.name: input_tree_digest
fields.doc: The exact inputs the claim is about.

fields.name: base_generation
fields.doc: The version it was computed against.

structs.name: Receipt
structs.doc: Canonical bytes of what a publication was. Written before the commit that names it.

structs.name: StoreRequest
structs.doc: The service protocol request, carried in the inline payload of one call.

fields.name: op
fields.doc: StoreOp.

structs.name: StoreReply
structs.doc: The service protocol reply. The principal is never in it: it comes from the facet the kernel authenticated.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: StoreStatus.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: ResultOutcome.

golden.name: object_empty
golden.doc: An object of no bytes. Its digest is not the digest of an empty tree, because the type is inside the prefixed preimage.

golden.name: object_alpha
golden.doc: Ordinary content.
golden.content: ascii:alpha bytes for the k4 golden vectors

golden.name: object_beta
golden.doc: Short content, used where a digest is needed for something that is not a root.

golden.name: object_wide
golden.doc: Content wide enough that a record framing it spans more than one sector, which is what makes a torn write detectable rather than invisible.

golden.name: tree_leaf
golden.doc: A tree of three bytes objects in canonical name order.

golden.name: tree_root
golden.doc: A tree naming a subtree and a file whose executable bit is part of the version.

golden.name: policy_signed
golden.doc: A policy that requires validation and admits two of the four principals.

golden.name: validation_pass
golden.doc: A passing claim about exactly the inputs of `tree_root`, computed against generation seven.

golden.name: manifest_v8
golden.doc: The candidate root of the eighth generation: content, policy and evidence in one object.

golden.name: request_v8
golden.doc: The identity of the publication that produced generation eight, outbox intent included.

golden.name: receipt_v8
golden.doc: What that publication was, written before the commit that names it.

golden.name: store_uuid_a
golden.doc: The identity of the store this vector set describes.

golden.name: record_checkpoint
golden.doc: The checkpoint that opens arena zero, carrying two principals, one result and one retention.

golden.name: record_object
golden.doc: An OBJECT record framing the manifest: head, then the canonical bytes the digest is taken over.

golden.name: record_prepare
golden.doc: The prepare of the eighth generation. After this record is durable the identity may not be forgotten.

golden.name: record_commit
golden.doc: The commit that makes generation eight the published one.

golden.name: record_abort
golden.doc: A prepare that recovery resolved because no commit followed it.

golden.name: record_outbox
golden.doc: What the broker reported about the intent committed with generation eight: neither delivered nor known to have failed.

golden.name: record_object_wide
golden.doc: An OBJECT record whose payload crosses a sector boundary. A tear after the first sector leaves a header that no longer describes what follows it.

golden.name: superblock_live
golden.doc: The newer of the two superblocks: generation four, arena zero, generation eight published.

golden.name: superblock_stale
golden.doc: The older superblock. Both are valid; the higher generation is the one recovery adopts.

golden.name: harness_stop_after_commit
golden.doc: Scaffolding: the directive that ends the machine once a commit is durable and nothing after it is.
